samples.summary: DOCX attribute injection via `style.alignment`: the sibling sink in the very function this change hardened is still interpolated raw into `<w:jc w:val="..."/>`
samples.evidence:
This change hardened every color sink in `buildRunPropertiesXml` (lines 95-101) against exactly this attack, but line 123-125 of the same file still does `const align = style.alignment === 'justify' ? 'both' : style.alignment; ... parts.push(`<w:jc w:val="${align}"/>`)` with no `escapeXmlAttr` and no allowlist. `align` is emitted for any value other than the literal `'left'`.

Attacker path, traced end to end:
1. `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:wid/documents/:did/content` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:120) accepts the body after `assertValidBlock`, which checks only `typeof b.style === 'object'` (line 265-267) — no per-field validation of `style.alignment`.
2. `writeDocsRoot` → `serializeBlockStyle` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:143) stores `alignment` verbatim as a Yorkie attribute string.
3. Reading back casts it unchecked: `partial.alignment = attrs.alignment as BlockStyle['alignment']` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:158 and packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:220), and `normalizeBlockStyle` is just `{...DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE, ...style}` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:273) — no validation.
4. Any user who then exports that document to DOCX (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docx-actions.ts:50, or the CLI at packages/cli/src/docs/docx-export.ts:33) reaches `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` via docx-exporter.ts:186.

Payload `{"style":{"alignment":"center\"/><w:fldSimple w:instr=\"DDEAUTO c:\\\\windows\\\\system32\\\\cmd.exe\"><w:r><w:t>x</w:t></w:r></w:fldSimple><w:x w:val=\""}}` breaks out of the attribute and injects arbitrary elements into `word/document.xml` (and `header1.xml`/`footer1.xml` via buildHeaderFooterXml:366). The victim downloads a .docx from their own trusted workspace, so the injected field/DDE construct is opened with the trust of a first-party file. A co-editor using a modified client (or direct Yorkie SDK access) reaches the same sink without the REST endpoint.

Note the asymmetry that shows the defense is known: the PPTX exporter maps the same field through a closed lookup with a default — `const algn = ALGN[block.style.alignment] ?? 'l'` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:79) — and the DOCX *importer* clamps it to the 4 legal values (packages/docs/src/import/docx-style-map.ts:104-107). Only this export sink trusts it. Fix: an `ALIGN_TO_JC` lookup with a `'left'` default, mirroring the PPTX side (escaping alone would leave a schema-invalid `ST_Jc`).

samples.summary: The docs content PUT API validates only the *shape* of `style`, not its values, so arbitrary strings persist into the CRDT and reach unescaped OOXML attribute sinks
samples.evidence:
`assertValidBlock` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:254-306) checks `id`, `type`, that `style` is an object, and array-ness of `inlines`/`tableData.rows`/`cells` — deliberately, per its own comment, "just the fields the writer unconditionally dereferences". No block-style or inline-style value is validated. `writeDocsRoot` then persists them verbatim (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:143, 174-184).

This is the enabling half of the `w:jc` injection above and is the reason that fixing only the color sinks leaves the class open: every current and future string-valued style field that an exporter interpolates is attacker-controlled. Surveyed the whole DOCX/PPTX attribute surface for other reachable string sinks — `fontFamily` is escaped (docx-style-map.ts:70-73, pptx text.ts:300), `headingLevel` is coerced with `Number()` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:438, docs-tree.ts:409) so at worst yields `Heading NaN`, `verticalAlign`/`borderStyle` are cast unchecked (yorkie-doc-store.ts:251,257) but the DOCX table writer emits no `vAlign`/`tcBorders` (docx-exporter.ts:301-323), `image.src` never enters XML (only the zip + an internally generated rId), and DOCX emits no hyperlinks at all — so `alignment` is the one live string sink today. Validating style values at the trust boundary (or per-sink allowlists) would make that robust rather than incidental.
searchedFor: grep 'ALIGNMENTS|isAlignment|alignment ===|validAlign' across all packages/**/src (only layout.ts, the toolbar, and the docx export ternary match — no validator)
read normalizeBlockStyle (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:272) — plain spread, no validation
grep 'w:fill=|w:color=|w:val="${|srgbClr val=' across **/src/**/*.ts to enumerate every OOXML attribute sink

samples.summary: Slides shape-fill / border / theme color sinks still bypass the new shared normalizer, relying on escaping alone — schema-invalid `ST_HexColorRGB` from a hostile import survives
samples.evidence:
The change routes docs `StoredColor` text colors through `toRgbHexColor`, but `colorChildXml` still does only `escapeXmlAttr(c.value.replace(/^#/,'').toUpperCase())` for every other caller: shape/gradient fills (`solidFillXml`/`gradFillXml`, color.ts:39-58), table cell fills and borders (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/table.ts:118,128), outer shadows (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/effects.ts:22), and `themeToXml` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/theme.ts:83, whose `toSrgbHex` likewise only strips `#`). Those values originate from PPTX import, i.e. an attacker-supplied deck.

This is NOT an injection hole — `escapeXmlAttr` is applied, so a quote cannot break the attribute; the residue is an invalid `ST_HexColorRGB` that PowerPoint rejects (a DoS-flavored interop bug rather than a security one). Raising it only because the change's own rationale is "one shared normalizer backs every OOXML color sink", and these sinks were left out, so the invariant is not actually established repo-wide. Defer the interop weight to the correctness lens.

verdict.reason: Verified independently and every claim holds. docx-style-map.ts:123-125 interpolates `style.alignment` raw into `<w:jc w:val="${align}"/>` with no escapeXmlAttr and no allowlist, guarded only by a negative `align !== 'left'` check, so any other string (including one with `"`/`<`) is emitted verbatim — while the same file escapes the sibling rFonts sink (lines 70-73) and clamps the color sinks via toDocxHexColor (lines 95-101). The taint path is unvalidated end to end: assertValidBlock only checks `typeof b.style === 'object'` (docs-content.controller.ts:265-267); serializeBlockStyle stores alignment verbatim (docs-tree.ts:143); read-back is an unchecked cast (docs-tree.ts:157-158) and normalizeBlockStyle is a bare spread-merge that validates nothing (types.ts:272-274); docx-exporter.ts:186-189 passes block.style straight to the sink. The DOCX importer clamps w:jc to the 4 legal values with a 'left' default (import/docx-style-map.ts:101-108), confirming the closed-set defense is known but missing on export. This is unsanitized untrusted input in a markup-generation sink — injection, in-lane, and blocking; no guard makes it unreachable.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: no value-level validation of block/inline style exists anywhere between the PUT trust boundary and the OOXML sink. assertValidBlock (docs-content.controller.ts:265-267) checks only that `style` is an object; the global ValidationPipe (main.ts:65-72) is inert here because the handler takes `@Body() body: unknown` (metatype Object, which Nest skips) and no DTO class exists for the route. serializeBlockStyle (docs-tree.ts:139-150, used at :241/:258 from writeDocsRoot:517) persists `alignment` verbatim; both readers cast unchecked (docs-tree.ts:157-158, yorkie-doc-store.ts:220) and normalizeBlockStyle (docs/src/model/types.ts:272-274) is a plain spread that only fills missing keys. The value then reaches an unescaped double-quoted attribute at docx-style-map.ts:123-126 (`<w:jc w:val="${align}"/>`) via docx-exporter.ts:186 — in a file that demonstrably escapes fontFamily (lines 70-73) and normalizes colors (95-101), so the omission is real, not stylistic. The only alignment allowlist in the tree is on the import side (docs/src/import/docx-style-map.ts:104-107), which this path never traverses; searches for `justify`, `ALIGNMENTS`, and `sanitize|assertValid|validateStyle|normalizeAlign` across **/src/** found no other candidate. Attacker with document write access (workspace member / API key) injects arbitrary XML into a DOCX exported by another user — injection lane, major impact.

finding.summary: `style.alignment` is interpolated unescaped and unvalidated into `<w:jc w:val="…">` — the same OOXML attribute-injection sink class this change hardens for colors, three lines below the fixed code
finding.evidence: buildParagraphPropertiesXml does `const align = style.alignment === 'justify' ? 'both' : style.alignment;` then `parts.push(`<w:jc w:val="${align}"/>`)` for anything that is not the literal 'left' (docx-style-map.ts:123-126). Unlike `fontFamily` (escaped at line 70-71) and now `color`/`backgroundColor` (normalized at 95/99), `align` gets neither escaping nor an allowlist. BlockStyle.alignment is typed as a closed union, but the runtime value comes from the Yorkie tree attributes with an unchecked cast: `partial.alignment = attrs.alignment as BlockStyle['alignment']` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:220), and `normalizeBlockStyle` only spreads defaults (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:272-274) — no validation anywhere on that path. Attack: a collaborator with write access to a shared doc (or anything writing the tree attr, incl. the backend docs-tree serializer) sets the block attribute `alignment` to `center"/><w:pStyle w:val="x` (or `a" w:x="`); when any other user exports the document, DocxExporter emits that string verbatim into word/document.xml (and header1.xml/footer1.xml via buildHeaderFooterXml), closing the `<w:jc>` element and injecting attacker-chosen OOXML into a file other users open in Word. Note the PPTX exporter does allowlist the same field (`ALGN[block.style.alignment] ?? 'l'`, packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:79), which is the pattern missing here. Confidence is medium only because I could not confirm the Yorkie server accepts an arbitrary `alignment` attribute value from a peer client; the exporter-side sink itself is unambiguous.

verdict.reason: Sink is present exactly as described: docx-style-map.ts:123-126 interpolates style.alignment into `<w:jc w:val="...">` with neither escapeXmlAttr() (defined at :25, applied to fontFamily at :70-71) nor a normalizer/allowlist (applied to color/backgroundColor at :95/:99). The value is attacker-controllable: assertValidBlock in packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:265-267 validates only that `style` is an object, never `style.alignment`, so a PUT @Body() unknown (:120-126) persists an arbitrary string; docs-tree.ts:143 writes it into Yorkie tree attrs and :157-158 casts it back unchecked; frontend yorkie-doc-store.ts:220 does the same bare `as BlockStyle['alignment']` cast; normalizeBlockStyle (types.ts:272-274) only spreads defaults and rejects nothing. A payload like `center"/><w:pStyle w:val="x` therefore closes the w:jc element and injects attacker-chosen OOXML into word/document.xml (docx-exporter.ts:186) and header1.xml/footer1.xml (buildHeaderFooterXml, :109/:121) in a file other users open in Word. No guard makes it unreachable: the closed union at types.ts:103 is compile-time only and defeated by the casts. In-repo counter-patterns show the omission (DOCX importer allowlists the same field at import/docx-style-map.ts:104-107; PPTX exporter allowlists at slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:79). Injection / unsafe input handling — in the Security lane.
